title: Dates and Times with java.time
summary: Getting time right - Instant for moments, LocalDate and LocalDateTime for calendar values, ZonedDateTime and time zones, Duration and Period, adding and comparing, ChronoUnit.between, formatting and parsing with DateTimeFormatter, and a Clock for testable code.

cards.q: Which type should a server store for "when did this happen"?
cards.a:
An `Instant`, a moment that is the same everywhere

An `Instant` means the same moment for everyone; a zone is applied only when showing it to a person. A `LocalDateTime` has no zone, so it does not pin down a moment.

February has no 31st, so the result is clamped to the last valid day of the month

`plusMonths` moves the month and keeps the day if it can; when the day does not exist, it uses the month's last day.

cards.q: What is the difference between `Duration.ofDays(1)` and `Period.ofDays(1)`?
cards.a:
`Duration` is always 24 hours; `Period` is a calendar day, which can be 23 or 25

`Duration` measures exact time; `Period` counts calendar units, so across a daylight-saving change one day can be 23 or 25 hours.
